section.content: 本申请提供一种锂离子电池，其包括正极极片、负极极片、隔离膜以及电解液。所述电解液包括添加剂A以及添加剂B，所述添加剂A选自环状硫酸酯化合物中的一种或几种，所述添加剂B选自硅烷磷酸酯化合物、硅烷硼酸酯化合物中的一种或几种。所述添加剂A与所述负极活性物质的质量比小于等于0.05；所述添加剂B与所述正极活性物质的质量比小于等于0.04。本申请将环状硫酸酯化合物与硅烷磷酸酯化合物和/或硅烷硼酸酯化合物组合使用，可在满足混合动力汽车大功率脉充脉放使用需求的前提下，保证锂离子电池具有长的循环寿命，保证锂离子电池的可靠性。

The application provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, an isolating membrane and electrolyte. The electrolyte comprises an additive A and an additive B, wherein the additive A is selected from one or more of cyclic sulfate compounds, and the additive B is selected from one or more of silane phosphate compounds and silane borate compounds. The mass ratio of the additive A to the negative electrode active material is less than or equal to 0.05; the mass ratio of the additive B to the positive electrode active material is 0.04 or less. The cyclic sulfate compound and the silane phosphate compound and/or the silane borate compound are combined for use, so that the long cycle life of the lithium ion battery can be ensured and the reliability of the lithium ion battery can be ensured on the premise of meeting the use requirement of high-power pulse charging and pulse discharging of a hybrid electric vehicle.

Lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The application relates to the field of batteries, in particular to a lithium ion battery.

Background

Compared with lead-acid batteries, nickel-metal hydride batteries and nickel-cadmium batteries, lithium ion batteries have the advantages of high energy density, long cycle life and the like, and are widely applied to various fields at present. For Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV) applications, batteries are required to have low internal resistance, long storage life, and cycle life. The lower internal resistance is beneficial to the automobile to have larger charge-discharge power, better acceleration performance and power performance, and can recover energy to a greater extent and improve the fuel efficiency; the long storage and cycle life is for the battery to have long term reliability, maintaining good performance over the normal life of the vehicle.

Therefore, in order to meet the performance requirements of the hybrid electric vehicle for the battery, it is necessary to provide a lithium ion battery with good comprehensive performance.

Disclosure of Invention

In view of the problems in the background art, the present application aims to provide a lithium ion battery, which has a long cycle life and can meet the use requirement of high-power pulse charging and pulse discharging of a hybrid electric vehicle.

In order to achieve the above object, in one aspect of the present application, the present application provides a lithium ion battery, which includes a positive electrode sheet, a negative electrode sheet, a separator, and an electrolyte. The positive pole piece comprises a positive current collector and a positive active substance layer arranged on the positive current collector, and the positive active substance layer comprises a positive active substance; the negative pole piece includes the negative current collector and sets up the negative pole active material layer on the negative current collector, the negative pole active material layer includes negative pole active material. The electrolyte comprises an additive A and an additive B, wherein the additive A is selected from one or more of cyclic sulfate compounds, and the additive B is selected from one or more of silane phosphate compounds and silane borate compounds. The mass ratio of the additive A to the negative electrode active material is 0.05 or less, and the mass ratio of the additive B to the positive electrode active material is 0.04 or less.

Compared with the prior art, the application at least comprises the following beneficial effects:

according to the application, the cyclic sulfate compound, the silane phosphate compound and/or the silane borate compound are combined for use, the mass ratio of the two additives to the positive active material and the negative active material is respectively limited, and the long cycle life and the reliability of the lithium ion battery can be ensured on the premise of meeting the use requirements of high-power pulse charging and pulse discharging of a hybrid electric vehicle.

Detailed Description

The lithium ion battery according to the present application is explained in detail below.

The lithium ion battery comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, an isolating membrane and electrolyte. The positive pole piece comprises a positive current collector and a positive active substance layer arranged on the positive current collector, and the positive active substance layer comprises a positive active substance; the negative pole piece includes the negative current collector and sets up the negative pole active material layer on the negative current collector, the negative pole active material layer includes negative pole active material. The electrolyte comprises an additive A and an additive B, wherein the additive A is selected from one or more of cyclic sulfate compounds, and the additive B is selected from one or more of silane phosphate compounds and silane borate compounds. The mass ratio of the additive A to the negative electrode active material is 0.05 or less, and the mass ratio of the additive B to the positive electrode active material is 0.04 or less. In other words, in the lithium ion battery described herein, the mass of the additive a in the electrolyte needs to be 0.05g or less per gram of the negative electrode active material, and the mass of the additive B in the electrolyte needs to be 0.04g or less per gram of the positive electrode active material. Preferably, the mass ratio of the additive a to the negative electrode active material is 0.02 or less, and more preferably, the mass ratio of the additive a to the negative electrode active material is 0.005 to 0.02. Preferably, the mass ratio of the additive B to the positive electrode active material is 0.01 or less, and more preferably, the mass ratio of the additive B to the positive electrode active material is 0.005 to 0.01.

During the formation and film-forming process of the lithium ion battery, the potential of the negative electrode is reduced faster than that of the positive electrode, and the reduction potential of the cyclic sulfate compound is higher than that of the organic solvent, so that the cyclic sulfate compound preferentially forms lithium sulfite (Li) on the interface of the negative electrode2SO3) The residual cyclic sulfate compound not participating in the reaction of the negative electrode interface forms lithium sulfate (ROSO) at the positive electrode interface under high potential3Li) CEI film containing Li as main component, lithium sulfate (ROSO)3Li) has an alkoxy structure-CH in the main chain structure2CH2O-is formed. The silane phosphate ester compound and the silane borate ester compound have lower oxidation potential and lower reduction potential than organic solvents and can form Li on the positive electrode interface when in use3PO4、Li3BO3、LiBF4Inorganic salts, etc., preferably modify the CEI film formed on the positive electrode interface by the cyclic sulfate compound. Since the film-forming potential of the silane phosphate ester compound or silane borate ester compound at the negative electrode interface is lower than that of the cyclic sulfate ester compound, the cyclic sulfate ester compound preferentially forms lithium sulfite (Li) at the negative electrode interface2SO3) An SEI film, a silane phosphate ester compound, and Li formed at the interface of the negative electrode by a silane borate ester compound3PO4、Li3BO3、LiBF4Inorganic salt substances are not beneficial to the stability of an SEI film in the long-term high-temperature cycle process of the lithium ion battery, and the high-temperature cycle life of the lithium ion battery is easy to deteriorate, so that the addition amounts of the silane phosphate ester compound and the silane borate ester compound are proper. According to the method, a certain amount of cyclic sulfate compound is added into the electrolyte, so that a stable SEI film is formed on a negative electrode interface, a CEI film formed on a positive electrode interface is prevented from being too thick, a certain amount of silane phosphate compound and silane borate compound are added to modify the CEI film formed on the positive electrode interface by the cyclic sulfate compound, the lithium ion mobility is improved, the impedance of the positive electrode interface is further reduced, the situation that the lithium ion mobility is reduced due to the fact that the too thick CEI film is formed on the positive electrode interface by the cyclic sulfate compound is avoided, and the charging and discharging power of the lithium ion battery is improved; meanwhile, the content of the silane phosphate ester compound and the silane borate ester compound is controlled to be preferentially consumed at the interface of the positive electrode, and a small amount of Li which influences the stability of the SEI film of the negative electrode in the high-temperature cycle process is formed or is not generated at the interface of the negative electrode3PO4、Li3BO3、LiBF4And inorganic salt substances are added, so that the charge and discharge power of the lithium ion battery is improved, and the good high-temperature cycle life is ensured.

The amount of the cyclic sulfate compound added is not preferably too high, and in the present application, the mass of the cyclic sulfate compound in the electrolyte per gram of the negative electrode active material is 0.05g or less, preferably, the mass of the cyclic sulfate compound in the electrolyte per gram of the negative electrode active material is 0.02g or less, and further preferably, the cyclic sulfate compound in the electrolyte per gram of the negative electrode active materialThe mass of the cyclic sulfate compound is 0.005g to 0.02 g. Thus, the cyclic sulfate compound can be ensured to form low-impedance and high-stability lithium sulfite (Li) mainly at the interface of the negative electrode2SO3) The SEI film which is the main component can avoid the formation of over-thick lithium sulfate (ROSO) at the interface of the positive electrode3Li) is taken as a main component, thereby improving the mobility of lithium ions, ensuring that the lithium ion battery has higher charge and discharge power and good cycle life.

The addition amount of the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound is not also preferably too high, and in the present application, the mass of the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound per gram of the positive electrode active material is 0.04g or less, preferably the mass of the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound per gram of the positive electrode active material is 0.01g or less, and more preferably the mass of the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound per gram of the positive electrode active material is 0.005g to 0.01 g. Thus, the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound can be ensured to form Li basically at the interface of the positive electrode3PO4、Li3BO3、LiBF4Inorganic salt substances are used for modifying a CEI film formed by the cyclic sulfate compound on the interface of the positive electrode to improve the mobility of lithium ions, and excessive Li formed on the interface of the negative electrode is avoided3PO4、Li3BO3、LiBF4Inorganic salt substances are added, so that the stability of the SEI film on the interface of the negative electrode in high-temperature circulation is improved, and the lithium ion battery has high charge and discharge power and good cycle life.

In the lithium ion battery of the present application, the content of the positive active material is not limited and may be selected as needed. Preferably, the mass ratio of the positive electrode active material in the positive electrode active material layer is 90% to 98%, so as to obtain a lithium ion battery with high energy density.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the content of the negative electrode active material is not limited and may be selected as needed. Preferably, the mass ratio of the negative electrode active material in the negative electrode active material layer is 93% to 98%, so as to obtain a lithium ion battery with high energy density.

In the lithium ion battery, the coating weight of the positive electrode active material layer on one surface of the positive electrode current collector is 0.001g/cm2～0.015g/cm2. The coating weight of the negative electrode active material layer on one surface of the negative electrode current collector was 0.0005g/cm2～0.01g/cm2. The coating weight test method comprises the following steps: taking 20 current collector foils, wherein the area of each foil is S, respectively weighing the weight of each foil, and taking the average value of the weight M1(ii) a Coating the same weight of slurry on one side of each current collector foil, drying at 120 ℃ for 1 hour after uniform coating, detecting that the current collector foil does not contain solvent basically, weighing the dried current collector foil with the slurry coated on one side, and taking the average value as M2(ii) a The coating weight M of the active material layer on one side of the current collector3＝(M2-M1)/S。

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the electrolyte further includes a lithium salt and an organic solvent.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the specific type of the lithium salt is not particularly limited, and may be selected according to actual requirements. Preferably, the lithium salt is selected from one or more of the following compounds: lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF)6) Lithium bistrifluoromethanesulfonylimide (LiN (CF)3SO2)2Abbreviated as LiTFSI), lithium perchlorate (LiClO)4) Lithium hexafluoroarsenate (LiAsF)6) Lithium bis (oxalato) borate (LiB (C)2O4)2Abbreviated as LiBOB), lithium trifluoromethanesulfonate (LiCF)3SO3). The content of the lithium salt is not particularly limited, and may be selected according to actual requirements, for example, a conventional addition amount may be selected. Preferably, the molar concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte is 0.5The molar concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte is preferably 0.9 to 1.3 mol/L.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the specific type of the organic solvent is not particularly limited, and may be selected according to actual needs. In particular, one or more of non-aqueous organic solvents are selected. Specifically, the non-aqueous organic solvent may be one or more selected from ethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate, dimethyl carbonate, diethyl carbonate, ethyl methyl carbonate, γ -butyrolactone, methyl formate, ethyl propionate, propyl propionate, and tetrahydrofuran.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the preparation method of the electrolyte is not particularly limited, and the electrolyte can be prepared according to a conventional method as long as the materials in the electrolyte are uniformly mixed. For example, a lithium salt, a cyclic sulfate compound, a silane phosphate compound, and a silane borate compound are added to an organic solvent and mixed to obtain an electrolytic solution. The order of addition of the materials is not particularly limited. Preferably, the electrolyte may be obtained by adding the lithium salt to the organic solvent, and then adding the cyclic sulfate compound, the silane phosphate compound, and the silane borate compound to the organic solvent together to mix them. Methods of making lithium ion batteries are also well known in the art, and the lithium ion batteries described herein can be made according to existing methods of making lithium ion batteries.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the electrolyte may also contain other additives that improve the battery performance: for example, additives for reducing the impedance of the positive and negative electrodes, specifically, lithium difluorophosphate, lithium tetrafluoroborate, lithium difluorooxalato borate, phosphoric acid anhydride, and the like; additives for inhibiting the growth of DCR in the circulation process, such as lithium bis (oxalato) difluorophosphate and the like; and additives for improving the safety performance of the battery, such as flame retardant additives like cyclophosphazene and fluorophosphate, or anti-overcharge additives like tert-butyl benzene and tert-amyl benzene.

In the lithium ion battery described in the present application, the specific types of the positive electrode active materials are not particularly limited, and are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected as required.Preferably, the positive electrode active material is selected from lithium cobaltate, lithium iron phosphate, lithium manganate, lithium nickel manganese cobalt ternary material (LiNi)1-x-yCoxMnyO2Wherein x is more than or equal to 0 and less than or equal to 0.5, y is more than or equal to 0 and less than or equal to 0.5, and x + y is more than or equal to 0.4 and less than or equal to 0.7). In particular, the lithium nickel manganese cobalt ternary material may be selected from LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2、LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2、LiNi0.5Co0.25Mn0.25O2、LiNi0.4Co0.2Mn0.4O2、LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2One or more of them.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the positive electrode active material layer further includes a binder and a conductive agent. The specific types of the binder and the conductive agent are not particularly limited, and are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Specifically, the binder can be one or more of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR) and sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC); the conductive agent can be one or more selected from superconducting carbon, carbon nano tubes, graphene and carbon nano fibers.

In the lithium ion battery, the specific types of the positive current collector are not particularly limited, are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Preferably, the positive electrode collector may be an aluminum foil.

In the lithium ion battery, the specific types of the negative active materials are not particularly limited, are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Preferably, the negative active material may be selected from metallic lithium, natural graphite, artificial graphite, mesophase micro carbon spheres (abbreviated as MCMB), hard carbon, soft carbon, silicon-carbon composite, Li-Sn alloy, Li-Sn-O alloy, Sn, SnO2Spinel-structured lithiated TiO2-Li4Ti5O12And one or more of Li-Al alloy.

In the lithium ion battery described herein, the negative electrode active material layer further includes a binder and a conductive agent. The specific types of the binder and the conductive agent are not particularly limited, and are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Preferably, the binder can be selected from one or more of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR) and sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC); the conductive agent can be one or more selected from superconducting carbon, carbon nano tubes, graphene and carbon nano fibers.

In the lithium ion battery, the specific types of the negative current collectors are not particularly limited, are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Preferably, the negative electrode current collector may be a copper foil.

In the lithium ion battery, the specific types of the isolating membranes are not particularly limited, are all conventional raw materials, and can be selected according to requirements. Preferably, the separator may be selected from polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, and multi-layer composite films of the above polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride.

In order to make the purpose, technical solution and beneficial technical effects of the present application clearer, the present application is further described in detail with reference to specific examples and comparative examples. It should be understood that the specific embodiments described in this specification are for purposes of explanation only and are not intended to limit the application. The formulation, proportions, etc. of the examples can be selected according to local circumstances without substantially affecting the results.

The lithium ion batteries of examples 1 to 14 and comparative examples 1 to 5 were each prepared according to the following preparation method.

(1) Preparation of positive pole piece

Reacting LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2Mixing polyvinylidene fluoride and acetylene black according to the mass ratio of 91:4:5, adding the mixture into an N-methyl pyrrolidone (NMP) solvent, and uniformly stirring the mixture under the action of a vacuum stirrer to obtain anode slurry; uniformly coating the positive electrode slurry on an aluminum foil with the thickness of 12 mu m; and (3) airing the aluminum foil at room temperature, transferring the aluminum foil to a 120 ℃ oven for drying for 1h, forming a positive active material layer by using the positive slurry, and then performing cold pressing and slitting to obtain the positive pole piece.

(2) Preparation of negative pole piece

Mixing artificial graphite, acetylene black, sodium carboxymethylcellulose and styrene butadiene rubber emulsion according to the mass ratio of 94:2:2:2, adding the mixture into a deionized water solvent, and uniformly stirring the mixture under the action of a vacuum stirrer to obtain negative electrode slurry; uniformly coating the negative electrode slurry on a copper foil with the thickness of 8 mu m; and (3) airing the copper foil at room temperature, transferring the copper foil to a 120 ℃ oven for drying for 1h, forming a negative active material layer by using the negative slurry, and then performing cold pressing and slitting to obtain the negative pole piece.

(3) Preparation of the electrolyte

In a drying room, weighing and mixing organic solvents according to the mass ratio of Ethylene Carbonate (EC) to methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) to 3:7, and then adding lithium salt LiPF6And then adding an additive, and uniformly mixing to obtain an electrolyte, wherein the molar concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte is 1 mol/L.

The kinds and contents of the respective additives are shown in tables 1 and 2. Wherein, the content of the cyclic sulfate compound is based on the mass corresponding to each gram of the negative electrode active substance, and the content of the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound is based on the mass corresponding to each gram of the positive electrode active substance.

(4) Preparation of lithium ion battery

Separating the positive pole piece and the negative pole piece by using a polypropylene isolating film with the thickness of 16 mu m, winding the positive pole piece and the negative pole piece into a square bare cell, then filling an aluminum plastic film, baking the film at 80 ℃ to remove water, injecting corresponding electrolyte, sealing the opening of the opening, and carrying out the working procedures of standing, hot cold pressing, formation, clamping, capacity grading and the like to obtain the finished product of the lithium ion battery.

Test I, normal temperature 40C discharge DCR test of lithium ion battery

The SOC of the lithium ion battery is adjusted to 50% at normal temperature (25 ℃), and the lithium ion battery is kept stand for 2 hours. Discharging at 40C current for 10s, and setting the voltage before discharging as U1Voltage after discharge is U240C discharge DCR ═ U (U)1-U2)/I。

Test II, low-temperature 10C discharge DCR test of lithium ion battery

Adjusting the SOC of the lithium ion battery to 40% at normal temperature (25 ℃), placing the lithium ion battery in a high-low temperature box at the temperature of minus 25 ℃, and standing for 2 hours to enable the temperature of the lithium ion battery to reach minus 25 ℃. Discharging at current of 10C rate for 10s, and setting the voltage before discharging as U3Voltage after discharge is U410C discharge DCR ═ U (U)3-U4)/I。

High temperature cycle life test for lithium ion battery

Charging the lithium ion battery to 4.2V at a constant current of 3C at 55 ℃, then charging at a constant voltage until the current is 0.05C, and then discharging at a constant current of 3C to 2.8V, wherein the first cycle is realized, the cycle charging/discharging is carried out according to the conditions, and the cycle number when the capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery is attenuated to 80 percent is recorded as the cycle life of the lithium ion battery. The capacity retention ratio of the lithium ion battery (discharge capacity corresponding to the number of cycles/discharge capacity of the first cycle) × 100%.

From the test results in table 3 above, it can be seen that:

comparative example 1, in which a large amount of silane phosphate compound was used, although the normal-temperature and low-temperature high-power charge-discharge DCR was low, the high-temperature cycle life was poor mainly because Li was formed at the negative electrode interface when the amount of silane phosphate compound added was high3PO4The SEI film modified by inorganic salt substances has good ionic conductivity, but the SEI film is unstable at high temperature and deteriorates the high-temperature cycle life.

Comparative example 2, in which more cyclic sulfate compounds were used, although the high-temperature cycle life was good, the DCR at the normal and low-temperature high-power discharge was high mainly because the excessive cyclic sulfate compounds formed an excessively thick positive electrode interfaceLithium sulfate salt (ROSO)3Li) in the CEI film, which is the main component, increases the interface resistance of the positive electrode, deteriorating the high-power discharge DCR.

The content of cyclic sulfate compound and silane phosphate compound in the comparative example 3 is more, and the normal temperature and low temperature high power discharge DCR and high temperature cycle life of the lithium ion battery are poorer.

Comparative example 4 additionally used a cyclic sultone compound which produced lithium sulfite (Li) in formation of a film in a lithium ion battery2SO3) And lithium sulfonate (RSO)3Li) is the major component, the high resistance SEI film, although making the high temperature cycle life of the lithium ion battery better, the high power discharge DCR is higher.

In comparative examples 5 and 6, the coating weight of the positive electrode active material layer and the negative electrode active material layer is large, so that the lithium ion mobility is influenced, the high-power discharge DCR of the lithium ion battery is also high, and the additive content in the electrolyte is not enough to effectively protect the positive and negative electrode interfaces, so that the high-temperature cycle life of the lithium ion battery is also poor.

In the electrolyte in the embodiments 1 to 14, the cyclic sulfate compound, the silane phosphate compound and the silane borate compound with appropriate contents are used, and the positive and negative active material layers with low coating weights are matched, so that the two additives are mutually induced during film formation, and the formed positive and negative protective films have high lithium ion mobility and are more stable at high temperature, so that the lithium ion battery has good high-power charge and discharge performance, low normal-temperature and low-temperature discharge DCR (direct current rating) and longer high-temperature cycle life, and has good comprehensive performance.

Therefore, the lithium ion battery can ensure that the lithium ion battery has a long high-temperature cycle life, particularly a long high-temperature cycle life at 55-60 ℃, has high normal-temperature and low-temperature charge and discharge power, particularly can remarkably reduce 40℃ discharge DCR at normal temperature (15-40 ℃) and 10C discharge DCR at low temperature (-15-40 ℃), and meets the requirement of high-power pulse discharge for HEV.
